headline.caveat: Minimum contracted lease payments over the initial 15-year term for 526MW of critical IT load at Helios (West Texas), leased across three phases; total potential value >$30B over 25 years assuming both 5-year extension options.

realized_to_date.caveat: Phase I (133MW) delivered and revenue-generating in 2026; cumulative rent received not broken out.

annualized_flow.caveat: Galaxy-guided average annual lease revenue >$1B at full 526MW delivery, at ~90% lease-level EBITDA margins.

nature_md: CoreWeave leased the entire converted Helios campus — 526MW of critical IT load across three phases — from Galaxy Digital under 15-year leases with two 5-year extension options (>$30B potential over 25 years; $10.4B minimum contracted over the initial term). Galaxy, a crypto financial-services firm, funded the bitcoin-mine-to-AI conversion partly with $3.5B of high-yield bonds and a $1.4B debt facility. Phase I (133MW) was delivered to CoreWeave in 2026 and is generating revenue.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: CoreWeave adds the Helios leases to its ROU-asset/lease-liability stack and passes costs through cost of revenue against customer contracts (Meta, OpenAI et al.); extension options are not liabilities until exercised.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Galaxy books lease revenue as capacity is delivered (>$1B/yr average at full delivery, ~90% lease-level EBITDA margin) against ~$3.5B of junk-bond funding — a leveraged landlord whose bond covenants rest on one tenant's credit.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** 90%-margin contracted revenue for 15-25 years transformed Galaxy's earnings mix overnight; Helios power rights were the scarce asset. **Bear:** single-tenant risk on a junk-funded conversion — Galaxy's Q2-26 slides tout a $30B pipeline while the firm posts losses, and CoreWeave's own credit (CDS ~50% implied 5-yr default, Jul 2026) is the true underwriting.
